approach: Before the first producer invocation in produce_and_verify (non-nested only), create a base-only snapshot, run the routed checks in it with an empty change list so none is skipped and none stops the run, and keep the failures by name as a Baseline. After the candidate's checks, a check that failed and also failed in the baseline gets `pre_existing = true` and a note saying it also failed on the base commit. Candidate checks continue past a baseline-failing check, so a later check can still fail for real. `CheckRun::blocks()` (failed and not pre-existing) replaces `passed` wherever the verdict, the checks line, or the verifier gate decides blocking. The `if all_passed` gate goes: the verifier always runs. The job is still rejected for a blocking failure, and every criterion is judged. The baseline is stored on the Verification record, so it is in the job's committed records. The verifier brief labels each pre-existing check. No config key.

decisions.choice: Mark pre-existing with a new `pre_existing: bool` on CheckRun (serde default, skipped when false), keeping `passed` truthful. Add `CheckRun::blocks()`.
decisions.reason: A pre-existing failure stays visible as failed in records and display. Old records still parse. One method gives verify.rs, run.rs and the brief a single blocking rule.

rejected.why: Hides the failure, and criterion 6 asks for a marker and a note.

rejected.option: A list of pre-existing names on Verification only
rejected.why: Criterion 2 asks for the marker in the check record.

decisions.choice: Fix the root cause: remove the `if all_passed` gate around the verifier, and drop the all-passed condition on the 'returned no verdict' reason in judge().
decisions.reason: The gate is why one unrelated failing check leaves every criterion unjudged. Judgment is the verifier's job whatever the checks say. The final verdict still fails on any blocking check.

rejected.option: Only open the gate when every failure is pre-existing
rejected.why: Does not meet criterion 4, which needs judging when an unrelated non-pre-existing check fails.

decisions.choice: Add a stop rule to routing::run_routed/run_local: baseline run = never stop; candidate run = stop at the first failure unless that check failed on the base.
decisions.reason: run_local stops after the first failure. A pre-existing failure early in the list (fmt, say) would otherwise stop clippy and test from ever running on the candidate, hiding a new failure.

rejected.why: Hides real failures behind pre-existing ones and baselines only the first failing check.

decisions.choice: Run the baseline in a fresh `Snapshot::create(.., SnapshotRepo::Base)` of the base, pin mounted, using the same check env and `SnapExec`, with an empty changed list.
decisions.reason: Same routed checks and runner, no candidate involved. An empty change list means skip_when_only (checks::skip_note) never skips, so a check the candidate later skips is still baselined. Skips are not pre-existing failures: they pass.

rejected.why: It does not exist until after the producer.

decisions.choice: If the baseline snapshot or runner errors, record Baseline::Unavailable(reason) and treat no check as pre-existing. A stop request (refuse_if_stopped) still propagates as an error.
decisions.reason: This follows the accepted reading. A failed baseline must never excuse a failure.

rejected.option: Fail the job when the baseline cannot start
rejected.why: Makes the new feature able to block jobs that ran fine before.

decisions.choice: Persist the baseline as an optional `baseline` field on the Verification record. Its status is ran or unavailable, with the base CheckRuns. It is emitted as a ui line before the producer starts.
decisions.reason: Additive and optional, so no schema bump and no new record type. It is committed with the job's other records. The ui line lets a test show baseline-before-producer ordering.

rejected.why: Needs AnyRecord, schema and parse plumbing, which is too big for one run.

files.purpose: Add `pre_existing` to CheckRun, `CheckRun::blocks()`, a `Baseline` type, and `baseline: Option<Baseline>` on Verification (serde default). Round-trip tests.
Set the new field in every CheckRun literal. Add a helper that marks a run pre-existing with the 'also failed on the base commit' note. Tests.
Add the stop rule to run_routed/run_local (never / except-baseline-failures / first-failure), also on the Fallback path. Tests.

Run the baseline before the first producer invocation (skipped when nested), print a `baseline` ui line, mark pre-existing after the candidate checks, remove the `if all_passed` gate, pass labelled check views, store the baseline on Verification. Use blocks() in the checks line.

Not in the brief's deliverables but needed: judge() decides blocking with `blocks()`, so a pre-existing failure no longer fails the verdict. A reason is added for blocking failures only, the 'returned no verdict' reason no longer depends on checks passing, and unit tests are added.
Add `pre_existing` to CheckResultView and render 'failed, pre-existing: also failed on the base commit' in the verifier brief. Tests.
Tell the verifier that a check marked pre-existing failed on the base too and is not the change's fault, and that it must judge every criterion even when a check failed.
Unreleased entry for the baseline, pre-existing marking and per-criterion judging.
Document `pre_existing` and `baseline` in athena.verification/1. It stands in for the deliverable docs/design.md, which does not exist.

steps: records.rs: add `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")] pub pre_existing: bool` to CheckRun, `blocks()`, the Baseline type (Ran(Vec<CheckRun>) or Unavailable(String)), and the optional Verification.baseline. Fix every CheckRun literal (checks.rs, routing.rs, run.rs nested branch, introspect.rs, reading.rs and verify.rs tests, drain.rs, briefs.rs as the compiler lists them). Add round-trip tests, including an old record without the fields.
checks.rs: add `mark_pre_existing(run: &mut CheckRun)`, which sets the flag and appends 'also failed on the base commit' to the note. Test it.
routing.rs: add `StopRule` and thread it through run_routed, run_local and Fallback. Update callers and tests; the default stays first-failure.

run.rs: after the producer snapshot is created and before the first agent_spec/invoke_and_record, when `self.nested.is_none()` build a base snapshot in a separate dir (e.g. job_dir/baseline, removed afterwards), route with an empty changed list, run with SnapExec and StopRule::Never, and collect Baseline::Ran. Catch non-stop errors into Baseline::Unavailable. Print a `baseline` line. Build check_env for the base snapshot with Side::Verify as the verifier does.

run.rs: for the candidate run use the stop rule that continues past baseline failures. Mark failures whose name is in the baseline as pre-existing. Compute blocking with blocks(). Delete the `if all_passed` gate so the verifier brief and invocation always happen. Pass the pre-existing flag and note into CheckResultView. Set Verification.baseline.

verify.rs: replace `!c.passed` / `all(|c| c.passed)` with blocks() (three sites). Drop the all-passed condition on the 'returned no verdict' reason. Add unit tests: pre-existing alone passes; new failure fails; criteria judged with a failing check.
briefs.rs and verifier.md: render and explain the label. Add a brief test.
lifecycle.rs: add the five tests using the fake agent. Check that existing tests still pass, especially the test-check deletion test (the base's test check passes there, so it stays blocking).
docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md. Run cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: The extra base snapshot and check run adds wall time and disk to every non-nested job.
risks.mitigation: The baseline uses the check timeout already configured, is removed after use, and the nested path skips it. The cost is accepted by the request.

risks.risk: Flaky checks fail on the base, then fail on the candidate, and are wrongly excused.
risks.mitigation: A check is excused only when it failed on both, matched by name. The note and the brief label make this visible to the verifier, which still judges the criteria.

risks.risk: A candidate could edit a check so it fails on the base only for a new reason, or rename it.
risks.mitigation: Checks come from the base's capability config and run against base tool config, as today. A renamed check does not match by name, so it still blocks.

risks.risk: The verifier now runs on every failed job and spends budget it did not before.
risks.mitigation: It runs under the existing verifier_usd budget and check_budget. The budget itself is unchanged, as required.

risks.risk: A literal-heavy change to CheckRun touches many files and may break an unseen constructor.
risks.mitigation: The field defaults and is skipped when false in serialization. The compiler lists every literal; cargo clippy --all-targets covers the tests.

risks.risk: Existing tests assume the verifier does not run after a check failure, for example the try-again carries-failed-output test.
risks.mitigation: The producer reruns the whole suite and updates only assertions about the gate, keeping the rejected outcome. The fake agent handles a verifier call.

demonstrations.method: New lifecycle test with the fake agent and a configured check that always fails. It captures the Lines output of `go` and reads the committed verification.json.
demonstrations.observes: A `baseline` line naming the failing check appears before the first producer line. verification.baseline lists that check as failed on the base.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no baseline step there is no baseline line, no `baseline` field, and the ordering assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: New lifecycle test (check failing on base and candidate) plus unit tests in verify.rs and briefs.rs.
demonstrations.observes: The check record has passed=false, pre_existing=true and a note containing 'also failed on the base commit'. The brief line for it carries that label. final_verdict is pass when the verifier passes and no other check fails, and the job is not rejected for that check alone.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without marking, the failed check makes the verdict fail and the job rejected, so the pass assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: New lifecycle test: the check passes on the base and the fake agent's edit makes it fail on the candidate. A routing unit test checks that a check later in the list still runs after a pre-existing failure and can fail.
demonstrations.observes: pre_existing is false, the verdict is fail, the state is Rejected, and the reasons name the check.
demonstrations.fails_without: If marking matched by name without requiring a base failure, the job would pass or be wrongly marked, and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: New lifecycle test where an unrelated, non-pre-existing check fails after a clean baseline, and the fake verifier returns a verdict for each criterion. A verify.rs unit test covers judge() with a blocking failed check and an output.
demonstrations.observes: The verifier invocation exists, verification.criteria has one entry per criterion with the verifier's evidence, the failed check is listed, and the state is Rejected. The reasons include 'check X failed' and not 'returned no verdict'.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the all_passed gate, no verifier runs and criteria are all 'the verifier did not assess this criterion', so the test fails.

demonstrations.method: The existing lifecycle tests, unchanged, plus a new assertion that the baseline has no failures and no check is pre_existing. A routing unit test checks that the stop rule for a base with no failures equals the old behavior.
demonstrations.observes: All checks ran, none has pre_existing, and the jobs land as before.
demonstrations.fails_without: A baseline that marked passing checks, or changed stop behavior, would break an existing lifecycle test or the new assertion.

demonstrations.method: Records round-trip tests in records.rs: a CheckRun with pre_existing and a Verification with a baseline serialize and parse, and an old JSON without the fields still parses. Read docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md.
demonstrations.observes: The marker and note are present in the record. docs/records.md describes `pre_existing` and `baseline` under athena.verification/1, and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] has an Added/Changed entry.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the fields the round-trip test does not compile or fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the full suite, then clippy and fmt. Each changed module (records.rs, checks.rs, routing.rs, verify.rs, briefs.rs, run.rs via lifecycle) has a new test.
demonstrations.observes: All pass. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any compile, lint, format or test regression fails the command.

open_questions: docs/design.md does not exist in the base. The plan documents the records in docs/records.md (and the changelog) instead; confirm that is acceptable or whether a new docs/design.md is wanted.

outputs.rs and display.rs are listed as deliverables, but I found nothing in them to change: the verifier's output schema is unchanged, and display.rs has no check listing. I left them out unless the producer finds a real need.

The baseline is stored on the Verification record, so a job that fails before verification (producer failure or admission refusal) keeps no baseline. Is a separate baseline file needed for those jobs?
The accepted reading says 'baseline unavailable'. I assume this is recorded as Baseline::Unavailable(reason), with a ui line.
